key_insight: An agent-guided multi-fidelity learning pipeline can detect and correct unstable GW-BSE calculations, improving quasiparticle and excitonic predictions without washing out real strain trends.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable high-throughput screening of optoelectronic materials by reducing the impact of numerical failures in expensive excited-state simulations.
method: Structural agent flags low-confidence or anomalous calculations across strain, stacking, and k-point branches.
Small sets of high-fidelity reference points anchor Gaussian process corrections.
Multi-fidelity transfer learns improved quasiparticle gaps and exciton binding energies with uncertainty calibration.
evidence_signal: Across strained MoS2-WS2 bilayers, the workflow identified spike-like excursions, near-zero-gap collapse, and cross-fidelity inconsistencies, and it improved agreement with higher-fidelity references versus a no-agent baseline.
watch_item: Performance depends on the agent correctly identifying fragile calculations; missed instabilities or poorly chosen reference points could still bias the surrogate.
paper_title: Agentic multi-fidelity learning of quasiparticle and excitonic properties
